short: The siege that ended the Roman state and made the Ottomans a European power.
full:
Mehmed II brought perhaps 80,000 men and a siege train that included a bombard cast by the Hungarian engineer Orban against a city defended by around 7,000. The Theodosian walls had held for a thousand years, but they had not been designed against gunpowder artillery. The bombardment opened on 6 April 1453. To get past the chain across the Golden Horn the Ottomans hauled warships overland on greased rollers and put them into the harbour behind it.

The final assault came before dawn on 29 May. Constantine XI died fighting in a breach and was never certainly identified among the dead. Mehmed entered the city that afternoon, converted Hagia Sophia into a mosque, made Constantinople his capital and took the title Kayser-i Rum, Caesar of Rome. Greek scholars carried manuscripts west into an Italy already reading them. Ottoman control of the eastern trade routes is part of why Portugal and Spain went looking for sea roads to Asia.
